decisions.rationale: Corviknight fainted, so pass. Volcarona (167 Spe) outspeeds both foes. Fire Blast is super-effective on Steel/Ghost Gholdengo and Grass/Ghost Sinistcha; damage range shows ~95% KO chance on64% HP Gholdengo. Targeting Gholdengo forces Sinistcha to either let it take the hit or redirect Rage Powder onto herself, where Fire is also SE. Quiver Dance is too risky at33% HP with broken Focus Sash, and Bug Buzz is0.25x into Gholdengo. Protect wastes the turn.
decisions.notebook: Durable core: Volcarona + Corviknight once Rock threat is gone. Never rely on Focus Sash below full HP; always KO Excadrill before it can Rock Slide. Corviknight should Protect vs spread/electric moves rather than weak Flying hits. Avoid fielding Medicham with Ground-weak allies. Prioritize Fire Blast on Steel/Ground targets; Quiver Dance only safe after Rock threat is eliminated. Against Rage Powder partners, target the ally to force redirection or hit through if they don't.

Good as Gold made Gholdengo a total blank to Mega Medicham (Close Combat/Fake Out) and it OHKO'd Medicham with Shadow Ball on turn 3, then removed Corviknight with Thunderbolt and finished Volcarona through its Sash with repeated Shadow Balls. The opponent also burned two full turns on double-Protect, giving free damage. Keep Excadrill in back only as an emergency Volcarona check (LO Rock Slide OHKOs it) and accept it is slow without sand; do not bring Tyranitar just to enab

reflections.summary: Lost because the preview stacked two Rock-weak attackers (Corviknight, Volcarona) into a Sand/Rock-Slide core (Tyranitar/Excadrill) while leaving Archaludon unused; Mega Medicham was instantly removed by Gholdengo Shadow Ball, and Volcarona fired into Sinistcha’s Rage Powder, missed, then died to Shadow Ball with no remaining win condition.
reflections.adjustment: For Game 2 revise the four: drop Corviknight, activate Archaludon, and either bench Medicham or hold Medichamite without Mega Evolving; open spread-safe, eliminate Excadrill before Rock Slide, and target Gholdengo—not Sinistcha—when Rage Powder is up.
reflections.notebook: Durable opponent: Sand Stream Tyranitar + Sand Rush Excadrill with Rock Slide spread—never pair Corviknight and Volcarona together. Gholdengo carries Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Leftovers; Medicham-Mega dies to Shadow Ball, so avoid Mega Evolving into this lineup. Sinistcha runs Rage Powder + Heatproof + Sitrus Berry paired with Gholdengo; hit the ally or break redirection instead of firing into Powder. Opponent reserves Rotom-Heat and Floette-Eternal—expect different coverage in later games. Archaludon was benched; evaluate Sturdy as a Rock-resistant pivot vs sand spread.
